result.question:
I'm worried that urgent work on Transformer 1 at site MAIN is stuck behind an overloaded technician. Give me the MAIN site's work order KPIs for the last 6 months, including backlog, overdue count and average completion time. Then list every open work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority, scheduled date and assigned technician, and flag which ones are overdue.

For each technician assigned to those work orders, count how many open work orders they currently hold at MAIN. Anyone holding more than 5 counts as overloaded.

Next, work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630.

If Transformer 1 is at Condition 2 or higher, do the following for any overdue work order on it that sits with an overloaded technician. Reassign it to the technician with the fewest open work orders at MAIN, choosing among those who have worked on Transformer 1 before and are not overloaded. Give it a start date within the next 7 days that avoids any day with 3 or more scheduled work orders at MAIN. If it is Condition 1, don't reassign anything. Just list the overdue items and recommend a catch-up order, ranked by priority and then by how late they are.

If every technician with Transformer 1 history is overloaded, don't reassign. Tell me who is least loaded and recommend bringing in outside help. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
result.answer:
Nothing else is needed — all the data is in hand. Here's the full picture.

## 1. MAIN site KPIs — last 6 months
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total work orders | 1 |
| Completed | 0 |
| Backlog | 1 |
| Overdue | 0 |
| Avg completion time | 0 hrs (no completions in period — not computable) |
| Priority breakdown | P1: 1 |
| Top asset by WO count | Transformer 1 (1) |

## 2. Open work orders on Transformer 1
| WO # | Description | Priority | Status | Scheduled start | Assigned technician | Overdue? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking); long description carries 3 addenda covering confirmatory DGA sample, planned outage, monthly resample and draft corrective oil-treatment WO | 1 | APPR (PdM) | **None** (no sched/target dates) | **None** (no wplabor, no lead) | **No** — cannot be overdue, it has never been scheduled |

## 3. Technician load at MAIN (open WOs)
No technician is assigned to any Transformer 1 work order. For reference, site-wide open load is:
- MECHTECH2 — 1 open WO (1000046, Pump 3 bearing wear)
- HVACTECH1 — 1 open WO (1000045, Chiller 6 condenser flow)

**Nobody is overloaded** (threshold >5). WO 1000051 isn't stuck behind a busy technician — it's stuck because it has no technician and no start date at all.

## 4. TDCG from latest oil sample (2024-01-19)
H2 2850 + CH4 7400 + C2H6 5470 + C2H4 16650 + C2H2 7 + CO 32 = **32,409 ppm → Condition 4** (>4630).
All six gases were non-null in the latest sample; nothing carried forward. Note the sample is ~2.7 years old — there is no newer DGA telemetry for this asset.

## 5. Reassignment decision
Condition 4 satisfies the "Condition 2 or higher" trigger, but the reassignment rule requires an **overdue** Transformer 1 WO sitting with an **overloaded** technician. Neither condition exists, so no reassignment was made. Additionally, the pool of "technicians with Transformer 1 history" is empty (the only Transformer 1 WO has never had labor on it), so the rule could not have selected a target even if triggered.

Least-loaded technicians: **MECHTECH2 and HVACTECH1, tied at 1 open WO each.**

## Recommendation
The real risk is a Condition 4 transformer with a P1 work order that has no owner and no date. I'd suggest:
1. Assign 1000051 now (MECHTECH2 is the natural pick given it's a mechanical OLTC inspection; HVACTECH1 is equally free) — or bring in an outside transformer/OLTC specialist, since no in-house tech has Transformer 1 history and Condition 4 typically warrants manufacturer involvement (already flagged in the WO addenda).
2. Schedule it within the next 7 days — the MAIN calendar for 2026-09-30 → 2026-10-07 has **0** scheduled WOs, so any day is clear; earliest practical is 2026-10-01.
3. Pull a fresh DGA sample as part of that visit — the current classification rests on a sample from January 2024.

Say the word and I'll assign the technician and set the start date on 1000051.
